**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Transfer and Servicing Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding our party (the Issuer/Depositor):

- **Text search for "exclusive"** surfaces only (i) the Cap Custodian "exclusive control" mechanics over the Cap Collateral Account (Article IX) and (ii) the *non*-exclusive jurisdiction provision in Section 10.6 — neither restricts our sourcing freedom.
- **Searches for "sole"** return only "sole remedy" / "sole discretion" / "solely in its capacity" usages, plus no hits at all for requirements-purchase or "shall not engage any third party" style language.
- **Section 3.1 (Engagement)** appoints Cellco as Servicer, and Sections 3.10/3.11 appoint it as Custodian and Marketing Agent, but none of these is expressed as exclusive. This is a structural single-servicer appointment typical of a securitization, not an exclusive dealing covenant.
- **Article VII** reinforces this: on Servicer resignation or a Servicer Termination Event, a Successor Servicer can be engaged, including an unaffiliated institution with a $50,000,000 net worth that services consumer receivables (p0335). So there is neither full-term lock-in nor the absence of a performance-based exit that would push toward walk-away territory.

Result: the clause set sits at the **preferred position** (no exclusivity on us), so no edit is warranted.
